captions.instagram:
How do the kidneys work?

Every day your kidneys squeeze about 180 litres out of your blood and quietly put 99% of it back. Zoom into a nephron, push plasma through a three-layer filter, watch ADH turn urine dark, and see how dialysis and transplants took over when kidneys fail.

→ Your two kidneys sit high at your back, and the right one is a little lower, under the liver.
→ A fifth of every heartbeat goes to them: about 1.2 litres of blood a minute.
→ Each kidney holds about a million nephrons: a tiny filter joined to a long, looping tube.
→ Blood pressure squeezes water, salt, sugar and wastes through a three-layer filter. Cells stay in.
→ A net push of just 10 mmHg makes about 180 litres of filtrate a day.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/kidneyclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do the kidneys work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Every day your kidneys squeeze about 180 litres out of your blood and quietly put 99% of it back. Zoom into a nephron, push plasma through a three-layer filter, watch ADH turn urine dark, and see how dialysis and transplants took over when kidneys fail.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/kidneyclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/kidneyclear

In this video:
• Two beans at your back. Two fist-sized kidneys, about 150 g each, sit against the back wall of the abdomen, the right a little lower under the liver.
• A million tiny filters. Each kidney has about a million nephrons (from about 200,000 to over 2.5 million).
• Filtering by blood pressure. About 55 mmHg of blood pressure, minus 15 from the capsule and 30 from blood proteins, leaves a net push of about 10 mmHg.
• Taking 99% back. The proximal tubule reclaims about two thirds of the salt and water and all the glucose.
• More than a filter. The kidneys steer blood pressure with renin, angiotensin II and aldosterone, answer ADH to save water, keep potassium and acid in range, activate vitamin D, and send EPO to make red blood cells when oxygen is low.
• When kidneys fail. Stones form when urine is too concentrated.
